question_stem:
A particle of charge $+q$ and mass $m$ is travelling with a constant speed of $1.6 \times 10^5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ in a vacuum. The particle enters a uniform magnetic field of flux density $9.7 \times 10^{-2} \text{T}$, as shown in Fig. 9.1.

{{figure:figure_9_1}}

The magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the initial velocity of the particle and perpendicular to, and out of, the plane of the paper.

A uniform electric field is applied in the same region as the magnetic field so that the particle passes undeviated through the fields.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State and explain the direction of the electric field.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Calculate the magnitude of the electric field strength.

Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The electric field is now removed so that the positively-charged particle follows a curved path in the magnetic field. This path is an arc of a circle of radius $4.0 \text{cm}$.

Calculate, for the particle, the ratio $\frac{q}{m}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.part_stem: The particle has a charge of $3e$ where $e$ is the elementary charge.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Use your answer in (c) to determine the mass, in $u$, of the particle.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: The particle is the nucleus of an atom. State the number of protons and the number of neutrons in this nucleus.
